newsitem.title: USA: Newmont offers $2 billion for Santa Fe Pacific Gold.
newsitem.headline: Newmont offers $2 billion for Santa Fe Pacific Gold.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp. said Thursday it offered to acquire Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp. for $2 billion in a tax-free stock swap that would create the largest gold company in North America.

Denver-based Newmont said it sent a letter to the Santa Fe board offering 0.33 share for each share of Albuquerque, N.M.-based Santa Fe Pacific Gold, one of the largest gold mining companies in North America.
Based on Newmont's stock price of $47.50 on Thursday, the offer would be worth about $15.80 a share to Sante Fe stockholders.

Santa Fe's stock was at $13.375 when trading in both issues was halted on the New York Stock Exchange pending the proposed merger announcement. It rose $2.875 to $14.75 at mid-afternoon, while Newmont fell 25 cents to $47.25.
"The combination of Newmont and Santa Fe Pacific would be a win-win proposition for the stockholders of both companies," Newmont Chairman Ron Cambre said in a statement.
In a brief statement, Santa Fe "acknowledged receipt of a proposal from Newmont Mining Corp. reflecting the terms publicly announced by Newmont Mining.
"There is no further comment at the present time," it added.
Santa Fe also pointed out it is one of the largest gold mining companies in North America with mines in Nevada and California and exploration offices and projects worldwide.
